examples.en: The interviewer saw through my nervousness.

examples.ko: 감독은 상대 팀의 작전을 간파하고 선수를 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The coach saw through the other team's tactics and swapped a player.
That friend can see through a lie right away.
My mom saw through my true feelings at once.

examples.ko: 상황을 빨리 간파하는 사람이 일도 잘해요.
examples.en: People who read a situation quickly also do their work well.

examples.ko: 문제의 핵심을 간파하지 못해서 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I couldn't grasp the core of the problem, so it took time.

explain: '알아채다'가 일상 대화의 말이라면 '간파하다'는 숨은 의도, 속임수, 약점을 꿰뚫어 볼 때 써요. 글이나 뉴스, 스포츠 해설에서 자주 나와요. 윗사람이 하면 '간파하시다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '알아채다' is the everyday word, while '간파하다' is for seeing through a hidden intention, trick or weakness. You often meet it in writing, news and sports commentary. For a respected person, say '간파하시다'.

en: be gullible; take someone's words at face value

examples.en: It was just a joke, so don't take it seriously.
My younger brother believes everything I say.

examples.ko: 친구가 장난으로 한 말을 곧이듣고 울었어요.
examples.en: She took her friend's joking words at face value and cried.

examples.ko: 광고에 나오는 말을 다 곧이들으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't believe everything that ads say.
That person's words are hard to believe.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 어른들 말을 무엇이든 곧이들었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I believed whatever adults told me.

explain: '곧이듣지 마세요'처럼 부정형으로 가장 많이 써요. 거짓말이나 농담을 의심 없이 그대로 믿는 느낌이 있어서 '믿다'와는 달리 속을 수 있다는 뉘앙스가 있어요. 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라 '곧이들어요', '곧이들으면'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the negative, like '곧이듣지 마세요'. Unlike plain '믿다', it carries a feel of believing something without doubt, so you might be fooled. It is a 'ㄷ' irregular verb: '곧이들어요', '곧이들으면'.

examples.ko: 담력이 큰 아이라서 밤길도 무서워하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is a gutsy kid, so he isn't afraid of night roads.
I tested my nerve on the scary rides at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 담력을 키우려고 일부러 사람들 앞에서 노래했어요.
examples.en: To build up my nerve, I sang in front of people on purpose.

examples.ko: 그는 담력 하나는 누구에게도 안 져요.
examples.en: When it comes to guts, he loses to no one.

examples.ko: 캠프에서 담력 훈련으로 밤길을 혼자 걸었어요.
examples.en: At camp, we walked a night path alone as a nerve-training activity.

examples.ko: 담력 없는 사람은 공포 영화를 못 봐요.
examples.en: People without nerve can't watch horror movies.

explain: 겁내지 않고 버티는 마음의 힘이에요. '용기'보다 무서운 상황에서 겁먹지 않는 느낌이 강하고, 비슷한 말로 '배짱'이 있어요. '담력이 세다/크다', '담력 훈련'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the inner strength to hold steady without fear. Compared with '용기', it leans toward not getting scared in frightening situations, and '배짱' is a similar word. It is used as '담력이 세다/크다' or '담력 훈련'.

examples.ko: 새로 정한 규칙이 영 마뜩하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm not at all happy with the newly set rule.

examples.ko: 그 제안이 그리 마뜩해 보이지는 않았어요.
examples.en: That proposal didn't seem all that satisfying.

examples.ko: 사장님은 내 계획이 마뜩지 않으신 눈치예요.
examples.en: The boss seems not to like my plan.

examples.ko: 마뜩한 집을 찾을 때까지 계속 보러 다녔어요.
examples.en: I kept going to see places until I found a house I liked.

examples.ko: 월급은 괜찮은데 일하는 분위기가 마뜩하지 않아요.
examples.en: The pay is fine, but I'm not happy with the work atmosphere.
There's no gift that suits me, so it's hard to choose.

explain: 대부분 '마뜩하지 않다', '마뜩잖다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 '마음에 차지 않는다'는 느낌을 줘요. '마음에 들다'보다 조금 점잖고 글에서 더 잘 보이는 말이에요. 긍정으로 '마뜩한 집'처럼 쓸 수는 있지만 흔하지는 않아요.
explain_en: It is mostly used with a negative, as in '마뜩하지 않다' or '마뜩잖다', giving the feeling that something doesn't satisfy you. It sounds a bit more formal than '마음에 들다' and shows up more in writing. A positive use like '마뜩한 집' is possible but not common.

examples.en: Surely that person wouldn't have lied, would they?
You can't possibly have finished eating already, can you?
Surely they won't come out when it's raining this hard, right?

examples.ko: 설마하니 이렇게 일찍 올 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I never thought you would come this early.

examples.ko: 설마하니 그 친구가 그런 일까지 하겠어요?
examples.en: Surely that friend wouldn't go so far as to do that, would he?

examples.ko: 설마하니 내 생일을 잊은 건 아니겠죠?
examples.en: You didn't forget my birthday, did you?

explain: '설마'를 조금 더 강조한 말이에요. 뒤에 '~겠어요?', '~ㄹ까요?'처럼 그럴 리 없다는 추측이나 의문이 와요. 말할 때는 보통 짧게 '설마'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a slightly stronger form of '설마'. It is followed by a doubtful guess or question, such as '~겠어요?' or '~ㄹ까요?', meaning it surely can't be so. In speech people usually just say '설마'.

examples.en: Children have a strong desire to own their toys.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 소유욕이 너무 커서 친구를 잃었어요.
examples.en: He was so possessive that he lost his friends.

examples.ko: 물건에 대한 소유욕 없이 가볍게 살아요.
examples.en: I live lightly, without a desire to own things.
Possessiveness makes a relationship uncomfortable when it goes too far.
Even puppies show possessiveness sometimes.
You shouldn't confuse possessiveness with love.

explain: 물건을 갖고 싶은 마음뿐 아니라 사람을 자기 곁에 두고 싶어 하는 마음에도 써요. '소유욕이 강하다', '소유욕이 없다'처럼 말하고, 사람에게 쓸 때는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 '독점욕'은 혼자만 차지하고 싶은 마음에 더 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It covers not only wanting to own things but also wanting to keep a person close to you. People say '소유욕이 강하다' or '소유욕이 없다', and when used about people it sounds negative. The similar '독점욕' focuses more on wanting to have something all to yourself.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 낮의 더위가 조금 수그러들었어요.
examples.en: When the rain came, the daytime heat eased a little.
As time passed, my anger died down a bit.
That controversy isn't dying down easily.
Once the wind dies down, the boat will leave.
Let's wait until the trend dies down.
My fever has gone down, so I'm okay now.

explain: 기세, 열, 화, 논란, 더위처럼 강하던 것이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '가라앉다'보다 '세던 것이 꺾인다'는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when something strong, such as momentum, fever, anger, controversy or heat, gradually weakens. Compared with '가라앉다', it feels more like something forceful losing its edge.

examples.ko: 이번 경기는 우리 팀에게 승산이 충분히 있어요.
examples.en: We have plenty of chance of winning this game.

examples.ko: 솔직히 말하면 이번 대결의 승산은 반반이에요.
examples.en: Honestly, the chance of winning this match is fifty-fifty.

examples.ko: 승산 없는 싸움은 처음부터 하지 않는 게 나아요.
examples.en: It's better not to start a fight you can't win from the beginning.

examples.ko: 승산을 높이려면 연습을 더 해야 해요.
examples.en: To raise your chances of winning, you have to practice more.
I asked why he was taking the challenge when he had no chance of winning.
When a chance of winning appeared, the players' faces brightened.

explain: '승산이 있다/없다', '승산이 높다/낮다'처럼 말해요. 이길 가능성을 따져 볼 때 쓰고, 경기뿐 아니라 협상이나 도전에도 써요. '승률'은 지금까지 이긴 비율이라서 앞으로의 가능성을 말하는 '승산'과 달라요.
explain_en: You say '승산이 있다/없다' or '승산이 높다/낮다'. It is used when judging the chance of winning, not only in games but also in negotiations and challenges. '승률' is the ratio of wins so far, which differs from '승산', which is about future chances.

examples.en: My childhood dream finally came true.
This plan will be realized next year.

examples.ko: 네가 말한 모든 소원이 실현되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope every wish you mentioned comes true.
Goals aren't realized by talking alone.
I cried to see the dream that had come true.

examples.ko: 그 약속은 생각보다 빨리 실현돼서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: That promise was fulfilled sooner than I thought, which surprised me.

explain: '이루어지다'가 일상 말이고, '실현되다'는 꿈, 계획, 목표가 현실이 될 때 조금 격식 있게 써요. 앞에는 '꿈이', '계획이'처럼 '이/가'가 와요. 스스로 이루려는 쪽은 '실현하다'예요.
explain_en: 이루어지다 is the everyday word; 실현되다 is a bit more formal for dreams, plans, and goals becoming real. The subject takes 이/가, as in '꿈이 실현되다'. The active form, making it happen yourself, is 실현하다.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 궁금해서 안달해 봤자 소용없어요.
examples.en: There is no use fretting just because you are curious about the exam result.

examples.ko: 그렇게 안달하지 말고 조금만 기다려 보세요.
examples.en: Don't fret so much, just wait a little.

examples.ko: 동생은 새 게임이 나오기만 기다리며 안달해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is fretting, just waiting for the new game to come out.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 안달하는 모습이 귀여웠어요.
examples.en: It was cute to see the child fussing for me to buy a toy.
Fretting will not make the work finish faster.

examples.ko: 그는 승진하려고 안달하다가 오히려 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: He was so anxious to get promoted that he actually made a mistake.

explain: 단순히 '기다리다'가 아니라 마음이 급해서 가만히 있지 못하는 느낌이에요. '안달이 나다', '안달을 하다'처럼도 말하고, 보통 '-고 싶어서', '-아 달라고' 같은 이유와 함께 써요.
explain_en: 안달하다 means being so impatient that you can't stay still. You can also say '안달이 나다' or '안달을 하다'. It usually comes with a reason, such as wanting something or asking for it.

examples.en: Watching the World Cup, patriotism arises on its own.
He is a person with strong patriotism.

examples.ko: 애국심은 말보다 행동으로 보여 주는 거예요.
examples.en: Patriotism is shown through actions rather than words.

examples.ko: 외국에 살면 오히려 애국심이 더 커져요.
examples.en: Living abroad makes your patriotism grow even more.
Advertisements often use patriotism.
The harder the times, the more people's patriotism comes together.

explain: 나라를 사랑하는 마음이에요. '애국'이 행동이나 태도라면 '애국심'은 마음 쪽에 더 가까워요. '애국심이 강하다/크다', '애국심을 키우다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of love for one's country. 애국 leans toward action or attitude, while 애국심 is closer to the feeling. Typical phrases are 애국심이 강하다 and 애국심을 키우다.

en: not daring to do something; being unthinkable

examples.en: Buying an expensive car is out of the question for me.
With such a small salary, overseas travel was beyond my dreams.

examples.ko: 언감생심, 제가 어떻게 그런 자리를 바라겠어요.
examples.en: How could I even dare hope for such a position?

examples.ko: 집 한 채 갖는 건 언감생심 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: Owning a house is something I wouldn't even dare to dream of.
In this situation, studying abroad is out of the question.

examples.ko: 그 큰 상을 받으리라고는 언감생심 생각도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I wouldn't have dared even to imagine winning that big prize.

explain: 형편이나 처지 때문에 감히 바랄 수도 없는 일을 말할 때 써요. '…은 언감생심이다'로도 쓰고, 문장 앞에서 '언감생심 꿈도 못 꾸다'처럼 부사처럼도 써요. 조금 예스럽고 겸손하거나 자조하는 말투예요.
explain_en: It is used for something you cannot even dare to hope for because of your circumstances. It works as '…은 언감생심이다', and also at the front of a sentence like an adverb, as in '언감생심 꿈도 못 꾸다'. It sounds a little old-fashioned, modest or self-deprecating.

examples.en: It was dark, so I mistook my friend for someone else.

examples.ko: 그 말을 칭찬으로 오인하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't mistake that remark for a compliment.

examples.ko: 직원이 저를 손님으로 오인해서 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: A staff member mistook me for a customer and greeted me.

examples.ko: 이 광고는 소비자가 상품 효과를 오인하게 만들어요.
examples.en: This ad makes consumers misjudge the product's effect.
Some people mistake kindness for romantic interest.
I hope you haven't misunderstood what I meant.

explain: '착각하다'와 비슷하지만 'A를 B로 오인하다'처럼 어떤 것을 다른 것으로 잘못 보거나 잘못 알 때 써요. 조금 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 많고, 일상 대화에서는 '착각하다', '잘못 알다'를 더 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Similar to '착각하다', but it is used in the pattern 'A를 B로 오인하다', meaning to wrongly take one thing for another. It sounds a bit formal, so it is common in news and writing, while in conversation people more often say '착각하다' or '잘못 알다'.

examples.en: My friend broke a promise, so I resented him.
Please don't resent me.
The child went into the room resenting the parents.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지고 제 자신을 원망하게 됐어요.
examples.en: After failing the exam, I ended up blaming myself.
Make your next plan instead of wasting time resenting.

examples.ko: 오래전에 헤어진 사람을 원망한 적은 없어요.
examples.en: I have never held a grudge against the person I parted from long ago.

explain: '원망하다'는 상대에게 섭섭하고 화난 마음을 오래 품는 거예요. '미워하다'는 싫은 감정 자체이고, '탓하다'는 잘못을 그 사람에게 돌리는 행동이에요. 보통 '누구를 원망하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '원망하다' is to carry hurt, angry feelings toward someone for a long time. '미워하다' is just the feeling of hating, and '탓하다' is the act of putting the blame on someone. It is used as '누구를 원망하다'.

en: guarantee; assure; vouch for; swear confidently

examples.en: I swear I'll pass this exam.
Nobody can guarantee the result.
He said so with full confidence.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 안 올 거라고 장담하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to be sure it won't rain tomorrow.
My friend vouched that it was delicious and took me to the restaurant.
Don't be so quick to say you're sure.

explain: '약속하다'는 앞으로 하겠다고 정하는 것이고, '장담하다'는 틀림없다고 자신 있게 말하는 거예요. 그래서 '장담할 수 없다', '장담하기 어렵다'처럼 부정형으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: 약속하다 commits you to doing something; 장담하다 is saying with confidence that something is certain. That's why it often appears in negative forms like '장담할 수 없다' and '장담하기 어렵다'.

examples.en: He hates the person who deceived him.
War makes people hate each other.
The hatred I held for so long slowly melted away.
I want to live without hating anyone.

examples.ko: 아이는 자기를 괴롭힌 친구를 증오할 정도로 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: The child was so hurt that he came to hate the friend who bullied him.

examples.ko: 사람을 증오하면 내 마음이 먼저 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If you hate someone, your own heart suffers first.

explain: '싫어하다 < 미워하다 < 증오하다' 순서로 점점 강해져요. 증오하다는 아주 깊고 오래가는 미움이라서 말할 때는 거의 안 쓰고 글·뉴스·영화 대사에 나와요. 일상에서는 '너무 싫어요', '정말 미워요'라고 해요.
explain_en: The strength goes 싫어하다 < 미워하다 < 증오하다. 증오하다 is deep, lasting hatred, so it is rare in everyday speech and mostly appears in writing, news and movie lines; in conversation people say '너무 싫어요' or '정말 미워요'.

examples.en: Look at the clues and try to deduce the culprit.
The detective stayed up all night reasoning out the case.
I worked out the story just from the picture.

examples.ko: 추리할 수 있는 단서가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: There is not a single clue to reason from.
If you reason through the situation, the answer will appear.

examples.ko: 말투를 보고 기분을 추리하는 건 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to figure out someone's mood from their tone.

explain: 단서를 모아 결론을 이끌어 낼 때 써요. 그냥 '맞혀 보다'와 달리 근거를 따져 본다는 느낌이에요. '~을/를 추리하다'로 쓰고, 명사 '추리'는 '추리 소설'에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: Used when you gather clues and draw a conclusion. Unlike simply guessing ('맞혀 보다'), it feels like weighing evidence. It takes an object ('~을/를 추리하다'), and the noun 추리 is often met in '추리 소설'.

examples.ko: 괜히 평지풍파를 일으키지 말고 조용히 넘어가요.
examples.en: Let's not stir up trouble for nothing and just let it pass quietly.

examples.ko: 평지풍파가 일어날까 봐 아무도 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: Fearing it would stir up trouble, nobody could say anything.
That one remark was the start of all the trouble.

examples.ko: 잘 지내는 가족에게 평지풍파를 만들고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to cause trouble for a family that's getting along well.
I'm glad the matter ended without any fuss.
A small mistake grew into a big commotion.

explain: 평화로웠던 곳에 갑자기 생긴 소란이나 분쟁을 가리키는 한자성어예요. 주로 '평지풍파를 일으키다/일으키지 마'처럼 쓰고, 괜한 문제를 만든다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom refers to a sudden disturbance or dispute in a place that was peaceful. It is mostly used as '평지풍파를 일으키다' or '평지풍파를 일으키지 마', with a critical tone about causing needless trouble.

en: be deluded; be deceived; be misled

examples.ko: 광고에 현혹돼서 필요 없는 물건을 샀어요.
examples.en: I was taken in by an ad and bought something I didn't need.
Be careful not to be misled by fancy words.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 가짜 뉴스에 쉽게 현혹돼요.
examples.en: Many people are easily deceived by fake news.

examples.ko: 겉모습에 현혹되면 진짜 좋은 것을 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're misled by appearances, you may miss the truly good thing.

examples.ko: 그는 달콤한 약속에 현혹되어 큰돈을 잃었어요.
examples.en: He was lured by sweet promises and lost a lot of money.

examples.ko: 동생은 친구의 말에 현혹돼서 계획을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was swayed by a friend's words and changed the plan.

explain: 보통 '~에 현혹되다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 광고, 말, 겉모습처럼 마음을 흔드는 것 때문에 판단이 흐려진다는 나쁜 뜻이에요. '속다'보다 마음이 홀린 느낌이 강해요. 시험이나 글에서 '현혹되지 마라'라는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is usually used with the particle '에' as in '~에 현혹되다', and has a negative sense of judgment being clouded by things like ads, words or appearances. It feels more like being enchanted than simply '속다' (to be tricked). It often appears in writing and exams as '현혹되지 마라'.
